threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus stops at the oddest places. The locals know it’s the only way to catch a ride on a rainy day.
Last night on the 333, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old school R&B. Even the driver was chuckling. Best entertainment I've had in ages!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a guy playing sax on the bus, and the whole car started clapping. That’s when I felt the real Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you’re in Friedrichshain when the local kebab shop doubles as a late-night gallery, showcasing artists while your döner is sizzling.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know to keep their head down during a BART delay; tourists act like it’s a night at the museum when the trains stop.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 30-Stockton handed a breadstick to a tourist. He said, 'Welcome to San Francisco!' Traffic stopped for a moment, but it felt like a warm hug.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but real locals treasure the quiet corners where kids play and neighbors chat over old-school cafés.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the overwhelming excitement over trying pa amb tomàquet for the first time at a local bar. Classic sign.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus is more reliable than the Tube—wait until the next strike hits and your optimism crumbles.
Caught a late 196 bus last night, and a lad serenaded the whole bus with 'Wonderwall' on repeat. Never heard an old lady shush so loud.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I found a hidden café behind a laundromat, where the barista knew my order before I did. That’s when Neukölln felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you see spontaneous open-air concerts between kebab shops on a random Tuesday. It's like the city's heartbeat becomes music.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid the 14 Mission during rush hour but still insist on getting their tacos from La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a lady with a pet iguana on the 12 bus yesterday. The driver didn’t even blink. Just another Tuesday in SoMa.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas, but many locals prefer cafes for a quick cafe con leche with a croissant, especially before noon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their confusion at the Mercat de La Llibertat’s unique hours—most locals know it's closed just when you expect it to be open.
